predecessors.name: First Spanish Republic
predecessors.text: the Basque provinces (Gipuzkoa, Alava, Biscay) and Navarre, where 'the Carlists managed to erect a temporary state'

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: the Basque provinces and Navarre, retaken by the army in February 1876

ledger.x: 1873: Catalonia is fought over. the rebels 'controlled most of the Basque Country, Navarre, and Catalonia without opposition' (the page's sentence carries no year; it sits in the 1873 narrative after the cantonal rising; quote corrected by reviewer eu-20-n); in March 1874 the Carlists captured Olot and 'set their…
August 1873: the Carlists take Estella and set up a provisional government.
December 1874: the Republic ends with the Restoration ('in December 1874, a military coup installed a new Bourbon monarch', Alfonso XII); the contest over Catalonia goes on with the monarchy.
December 1874: the war goes on against the restored monarchy.

wars.name: Third Carlist War
wars.outcome: Government victory: Estella fell on 19 February 1876 and Carlos VII left Spain on 28 February 1876; the Carlists besieged Bilbao from 21 February to 2 May 1874 and failed.

certainty.note: A rebel state with moving front lines; the held ground shifted with every campaign and the cities never fell.
